editorial.headline: Pepper Farming With a Clear National and Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01281 covers integrated pepper farming, from land preparation to post-harvest work, and is nationally open to PMA at every business scale.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 01281 is a farming activity in the plain, agricultural sense of the word.** It covers pepper or merica cultivation under the Piper group, including the practical sequence that turns land into a producing crop: land preparation, sowing, nursery work, planting, maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest activity when those steps are carried out as one connected operation. The scope also includes cabai jawa or cabai jamu farming, as well as pepper seedling and seed-production activities. In other words, this is not merely trading pepper, processing pepper as a separate factory activity, or using pepper as a label for a broader food business. The record points to cultivation and the immediate farming cycle around the plant itself.

That matters for founders because this code is open across the full scale spectrum stated in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. A local operator can read that as a broad scale fit, from a smaller farming setup through to a larger agricultural operation. A foreign investor can read the national PMA position just as directly: the code is marked TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership ceiling of 100%. There is no partial cap in the record, so the national reading is clean. If the business activity really is pepper farming, including nursery, planting, maintenance, harvesting, and integrated post-harvest work, the national classification does not create a foreign-shareholding discount by itself.

Bali presents an equally clear picture, although the reason is different. The record says the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and that this activity is not blocked by the Bali moratorium. The reason given is specific: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, which means it is not blocked by the moratorium described in the record. That moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, permanently, but this activity does not fall into the blocked result stated here. So the honest lede is not a warning that foreigners cannot register it in Bali today. It is the opposite: based on this slim record, this pepper-farming activity remains nationally open to PMA and is not marked as blocked for Bali PMA registration.

The useful caution is therefore one of scope discipline, not invented licensing. The classification should be used when the business is genuinely farming pepper or cabai jawa/cabai jamu, including the cultivation chain and directly connected post-harvest work described in the record. The strength of KBLI 01281 is that the commercial story and the legal classification can line up without theatrical interpretation: a farm activity, open at all recorded scales, nationally open to full foreign ownership, and not stopped by the Bali PMA moratorium status shown here.
